Data Analysis

Data source

My data comes from the artists_2023.zip folder provided by Dr. Joy Lee, from where I downloaded the “Kendrick Lamar.csv” file.

Import data

library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)

library(readr)
Kendrick_Lamar <- read_csv("~/LUC/courses/2semester2/data science/DS_Spotify/Spotify_Kendrick/Kendrick Lamar.csv")
View(Kendrick_Lamar)

Data preparation

Since some tracks are duplicated, I have first cleaned them, and then removed live versions and Remixes of the same tracks.

Kendrick_Lamar <- Kendrick_Lamar |> distinct(track_name, .keep_all = TRUE)

Kendrick_Lamar <- Kendrick_Lamar |> filter(!grepl("Live at|Live Acoustic|Remix", track_name))

Kendrick_Lamar$album_name <- as.character(Kendrick_Lamar$album_name)

Album analysis (energy, valence and speechiness)

Since many of his albums are included in the file, I filtered for albums that have the highest number of songs in the data set.

Kendrick_Lamar$album_name <- as.factor(Kendrick_Lamar$album_name)

top_albums <- Kendrick_Lamar %>%
  group_by(album_name) %>%
  summarise(song_count = n()) %>%
  arrange(desc(song_count)) %>%
  slice(1:3)  # Select the top 3 albums

top_albums <- Kendrick_Lamar %>%
  filter(album_name %in% top_albums$album_name)

View(top_albums)
write.csv(top_albums, "top_kendrick_albums.csv", row.names = FALSE)

Valence level boxsplot

ggplot(top_albums, aes(x=album_name, y=valence))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Album name", y="Valence")

The album ‘good kid, m.A.A.d city (Deluxe)’ has the lowest medium for Valence level.

Energy level boxsplot

ggplot(top_albums, aes(x=album_name, y=energy))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Album name", y="Energy")

But for Energy levels, it has a relatively high medium.

Speechiness level boxsplot

ggplot(top_albums, aes(x=album_name, y=speechiness))+
  geom_boxplot()+
  labs(x="Album name", y="Speechiness")

All three albums have low mediums for speechiness level.

Kendrick Lamar’s most negative song

His top 3 most negative tracks:

Kendrick_Lamar |> slice_min(valence, n=3) |> dplyr::select(track_name, album_name, album_release_year, valence) |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)
track_name album_name album_release_year valence
untitled 02 | 06.23.2014. untitled unmastered. 2016 0.09
Bitch, Don’t Kill My Vibe good kid, m.A.A.d city (Deluxe) 2012 0.10
untitled 01 | 08.19.2014. untitled unmastered. 2016 0.11

His top 3 least energetic tracks:

Kendrick_Lamar |> slice_min(energy, n=3) |> dplyr::select(track_name, album_name, album_release_year, energy) |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)
track_name album_name album_release_year energy
untitled 04 | 08.14.2014. untitled unmastered. 2016 0.13
BLOOD. DAMN. COLLECTORS EDITION. 2017 0.24
Crown Mr. Morale & The Big Steppers 2022 0.24

‘Crown’ seems to be his saddest song, interestingly, in the album of Mr. Morale & The Big Steppers (2022) which has the highest medium for Valence level. Is that a lyrics intensive track?

His top 3 tracks with the smallest presence of spoken words:

Kendrick_Lamar |> slice_min(speechiness, n=3) |> dplyr::select(track_name, album_name, album_release_year, speechiness) |> knitr::kable(digits = 2)
track_name album_name album_release_year speechiness
Crown Mr. Morale & The Big Steppers 2022 0.04
Alien Girl (Today W/ Her) Overly Dedicated 2010 0.04
untitled 06 | 06.30.2014. untitled unmastered. 2016 0.05

‘Crown’ seems to be his saddest track, witch also has the lowest presence of spoken word:

Crown (2022, Youtube link

About ‘Crown’ :

  • his contrasting feelings about being seen and doing his best as a leader in his community while – obviously – not being able to please everyone

  • the crown imagery on the album’s cover where Kendrick – a Christian himself – wears a crown of thorn, a key symbols of Jesus Christ
